sources.title: Laurent Dubois, Avengers of the New World: The Story of the Haitian Revolution (2004)

leadership_drive.rationale: Rose from enslaved coachman to Commander-in-Chief and Governor-General of Saint-Domingue, documented via the extensive military and administrative record of the Haitian Revolution.

analytical_rigor.rationale: Employed documented sophisticated guerrilla and conventional tactics adapted to fighting Spanish, French, and British forces in succession, per Dubois's military account of the campaigns.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Led an armed uprising of enslaved people against colonial military powers — a specific, documented, extreme risk given the near-universal historical consequence of failed slave rebellions.

planning_orientation.rationale: Coordinated multi-front military and political campaigns across roughly a decade, documented via the surviving campaign record.

independent_thinking.rationale: Switched allegiance from Spain to France in 1794 based on his own strategic assessment of which side would better serve abolition, a documented, consequential judgment against his existing alliance.

adaptability.rationale: Shifted alliances (initially Spanish-aligned, then French) as circumstances changed, and adapted tactics against successively different colonial opponents — documented across the full campaign.

persuasiveness.rationale: Negotiated alliances and rallied a formerly enslaved population into an organized military and political force, documented via the revolution's own organizational history.

decisiveness.rationale: The 1794 switch from Spanish to French allegiance was a specific, dated, high-stakes decision documented in the historical record.

persistence.rationale: Sustained the revolutionary struggle across roughly a decade (1791-1802) against a sequence of different opponents.

discipline.rationale: Organized and trained a functioning, disciplined military force from formerly enslaved people with limited resources, documented via Dubois's account of the army's development.

proactive_agency.rationale: Initiated and led the movement's military and political direction rather than serving as one participant among many, documented via his rise to sole command.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained armed conflict against multiple colonial powers across roughly a decade rather than seeking early accommodation.

autonomy_need.rationale: Increasingly governed Saint-Domingue with growing practical autonomy from French colonial authority, documented via his later administrative actions.

collaboration.rationale: Worked alongside other revolutionary leaders (Dessalines, Christophe), though the historical record also documents real strategic friction with some of them — a genuinely mixed pattern, scored toward the center.

achievement_drive.rationale: Rose from slavery to become de facto ruler of Saint-Domingue and drafted its 1801 constitution, documented via the well-recorded political history of the Haitian Revolution.

resourcefulness.rationale: Built a functioning military and administrative structure from severely limited resources amid ongoing war, documented via the revolution's logistical history.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Real output in both military command and political governance (drafting Saint-Domingue's 1801 constitution), not military leadership alone.

systems_abstraction.rationale: Drafted a formal constitution for Saint-Domingue in 1801, a documented, genuinely systematic governance framework rather than ad hoc rule.

deep_focus.rationale: Sustained a multi-year military and political campaign (the Haitian Revolution) requiring continuous strategic attention across shifting alliances and battles, documented via the well-recorded campaign history.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Developed from a formerly enslaved plantation worker into a self-taught military commander and eventually governor-general, a documented trajectory of expanding capability across his life.

opportunity_sensing.rationale: Recognized and used the political instability created by the French Revolution as a strategic opening to advance the uprising's cause, documented via the timing of his key strategic moves.

provenance.notes: Second-batch diversity pick: early_modern/19th-century-boundary, latin_america (Caribbean, currently unrepresented in this region), military/political-revolution domain not represented anywhere in the current roster. Passes inclusion_v1 cleanly — his achievement (leading and winning the revolution) is entirely self-built from an enslaved starting position, the opposite of inherited power.
